blindSummary:
Nothing relating to being trans is criminalised in this country, and the capital hosts both Pride and an organised march for trans visibility (March 2024) — public trans organising that proceeds without serious incident. Anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation and gender identity (2019 amendments). Counterweights: hate speech and hate crimes remain common with no effective justice-system response (per a regional monitoring body), social-media death threats are routine, and there is no legal gender recognition.

For a visitor: no legal exposure; small but functioning community; the usual street-hostility caution for this region.
blindOutOfScope: Justice-system non-response and the absence of legal gender recognition are resident-facing/climate.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition — resident-facing; the justice-system non-response affects resident victims.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country: hate speech remained serious with no meaningful state response despite countless reports (echoed by a regional monitoring body's country report); in September a basic criminal court in the capital sentenced a man to two years for assaulting an LGBTI activist, applying SOGI aggravating grounds; a regional anti-discrimination monitoring body called for a ban on nonconsensual intersex surgeries; an anti-gender movement gained ground, including campaigns against a school handout showing a gay couple.

Community-media report (March 2024): this country marked the trans day of visibility with a march for trans visibility in the capital, organised by a local trans-rights group; the coverage notes a worrisome trend of religious institutions being mobilised to scapegoat this small, vulnerable group.

Regional LGBTI-rights coalition review 2024: country submissions from candidate and partner states of this country's wider region (including this country) with their top priorities, feedback on a 2023 progress report by a regional integration body, and recommendations to that body.
A foreign government's 2019 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the SOGI section - anti-discrimination law, societal violence and discrimination against LGBT persons.

Overseas LGBT-focused newspaper (Oct 2023): economic analysis of the cost of anti-LGBTQ discrimination in this country and a neighbouring country, treating discrimination as an economic harm in the region.

Regional news outlet (Feb 2012): a regional legal-rights index for LGBTI people put this country at the bottom of its region with a score of -2 on a scale from +17 to -7 - the only country in the region in the 'red zone' of worst offender states, characterised there by gross human-rights violations and discrimination.

Regional news outlet (July 2014): this country's government submitted a constitutional amendment to define marriage strictly as a union of one man and one woman, ruling out same-sex marriage and gay adoption - needing two-thirds of MPs, with the conservative ethnic-minority party expected to provide the extra votes.
